draft.area: Where SAP data lands and becomes a reported number: ADF staging into ADLS Gen2, landing into Snowflake or Databricks, SAP-specific physical and semantic modelling, and the Power BI semantic layer where a measure diverges from the warehouse table.
corrections_to_my_facts: MATERIAL AND CURRENT, do not print the booklet without addressing it: Microsoft's own SAP CDC architecture page now carries an Important notice stating that a recent update of SAP Note 3255746 announces a security patch that blocks incoming calls to the ODP RFC API from third-party clients including Azure Data Factory's SAP CDC connector, and points to SAP notes 3255746 and 3439624. Microsoft's stated alternatives on that page are Mirroring for SAP Datasphere in Fabric (GA), SAP Business Data Cloud Connect for Microsoft Fabric, Copy Job in Fabric for SAP with an ABAP Add-on (stated as publicly available at Microsoft Build 2026), and partner solutions with Open Mirroring. A booklet written in August 2026 that presents ADF SAP CDC as a safe strategic bet without this caveat is wrong. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/sap-change-data-capture-introduction-architecture

Your ODP context list is incomplete. The documented parameter values for ODP context are ABAP_CDS, BW, HANA (SAP HANA Information Views), SAPI, plus SLT~<Queue Alias> where the Queue Alias comes from Administration Data in the SLT configuration in the SLT cockpit (transaction LTRC), plus ODP_SELF and RANDOM which Microsoft describes as used for technical validation and testing and typically not relevant. You omitted HANA. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/sap-change-data-capture-advanced-topics

Nuance on Checkpoint Key that changes how you write the guidance: Microsoft states 'To avoid conflicts, a unique ID is generated as Checkpoint Key by default.' The uniqueness problem you describe only bites when engineers parameterise a single data flow across many sources, or deliberately pin a static key. Microsoft also states the Checkpoint Key property is not shown at all when Run mode is 'Full on every run', because in that case no change data capture process is established. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/connector-sap-change-data-capture

Raw SAP application tables are not a first-class SAP CDC source. Microsoft lists the ODP source types as SAP extractors, ABAP CDS views, BW InfoProviders and InfoObjects, and 'SAP application tables, when you use an SAP LT replication server (SLT) as a proxy'. Direct table extraction without SLT is not on that list. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/sap-change-data-capture-introduction-architecture

Add to the 'Current limitations' pair you cited: both incremental run modes (fullAndIncrementalLoad and incrementalLoad) require the Key columns property to be populated with the keys of the ODP source object. Microsoft's wording is that both incremental load options require specifying the keys of the ODP source object in the Key columns property. This is not optional and it is the most common cause of a silently wrong delta merge. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/connector-sap-change-data-capture

One operationally important gap in your summary: the SAP CDC connector is supported for mapping data flow only, and as source only. The supported capabilities table reads 'Mapping data flow (source/-)'. There is no copy activity SAP CDC source and no SAP CDC sink. Any 'we will just use a copy activity' shortcut in a design review is invalid. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/connector-sap-change-data-capture

If your booklet mentions the ADF Snowflake connector: Snowflake V1 is documented as being 'at removal stage' and Microsoft recommends upgrading V1 to V2. V2 exists as version 1.0 and version 1.1, and the differences are behavioural, not cosmetic. V2 version 1.0 returns Snowflake NUMBER as a string in Lookup activity, reads TIMESTAMP_LTZ, TIMESTAMP_NTZ and TIMESTAMP_TZ as DateTimeOffset, and does not support script parameters or multiple SQL statement execution in Script activity. Version 1.1 restores script parameters and multi-statement execution and adds treatDecimalAsString. An upgrade done as a routine 'connector refresh' will silently change decimal and timestamp typing in downstream pipelines. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/connector-snowflake

Small precision point on the staging linked service: Microsoft's wording is that the staging folder 'should be considered an internal storage of the SAP CDC connector' and that 'the file format used for the staging data might change', with an explicit recommendation not to use the staging folder for other purposes, for example as a source for other copy activities or mapping data flows. Teams routinely treat that folder as their bronze layer. It is not one. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/connector-sap-change-data-capture

products.name: SAP CDC connector (mapping data flow source)
products.what_a_senior_person_uses_it_for: Establishing and owning ODQ delta subscriptions against ECC, S/4HANA, BW, BW/4HANA and SLT. The senior work is not building the data flow, it is governing the Checkpoint Key namespace across a parameterised fleet, choosing Key columns per ODP object, designing the JSON source partitioning scheme (arrays of {fieldName, sign, option, low, high} selection options, SAP internal format with leading zeroes and YYYYMMDD dates, non-overlapping because ADF performs no checks on these conditions), and knowing that debug runs use a different subscriber process value than triggered runs, so change-capture stability can only be proven with published, triggered runs.

products.name: Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2, as SAP CDC staging and separately as the governed landing zone
products.what_a_senior_person_uses_it_for: Two physically separate containers that juniors conflate. Container one is the SAP CDC staging folder, which Microsoft designates internal to the connector, whose file format may change, which cannot use a self-hosted integration runtime, and which must not be read by anything else. Container two is the actual landing zone written by the data flow sink, laid out with Hive-style partitioning, sized for the downstream reader, and registered to a Unity Catalog external location or a Snowflake external volume. Senior work is enforcing that separation in the ARM template and in storage RBAC, not in a wiki page.

products.name: Apache Iceberg tables and external volumes
products.what_a_senior_person_uses_it_for: Deciding, per table, between a Snowflake-managed Iceberg table (full platform support, read and write, but third-party clients cannot append to, delete from, or upsert it) and an externally managed one via catalog integration (limited platform support, no clustering, and Snowflake assumes no lifecycle management of the table). The external volume is a named, account-level object binding Snowflake to the ADLS Gen2 path. Senior work is knowing that Fail-safe, encryption, temporary tables and hybrid tables are unsupported for all Iceberg tables, and that cloning and standard streams work only on Snowflake-managed ones, which quietly removes several recovery and CDC patterns.

products.name: Catalog integration for Unity Catalog (Iceberg REST) and catalog-linked databases
products.what_a_senior_person_uses_it_for: Running Snowflake and Databricks over one physical copy of the SAP facts instead of two divergent copies. Snowflake documents that catalog-linked databases support both read and write by default against Unity Catalog Iceberg tables, authenticated by OAuth with a Databricks service principal or by a Databricks personal access token, using vended credentials or an external volume, and requiring EXTERNAL USE SCHEMA on the Databricks side when vended credentials are used. Senior work is deciding who owns the single write path, because two engines writing one Iceberg table is where the reconciliation story dies.

products.name: Snowpipe and COPY INTO <table>
products.what_a_senior_person_uses_it_for: Choosing between them on load-history semantics rather than latency marketing. Snowpipe keeps load history in the pipe metadata for 14 days and refuses a filename it has already seen even if the file was later modified and has a different eTag; COPY INTO's load metadata becomes uncertain after 64 days. Snowpipe splits a load across one or multiple transactions and gives no ordering guarantee, while a bulk load occurs in a single transaction. Senior work is designing filenames so a corrected SAP extract is a new name rather than an overwrite, reserving FORCE = TRUE for a deliberate, logged replay, and using MATCH_BY_COLUMN_NAME (CASE_SENSITIVE or CASE_INSENSITIVE) so Parquet lands without an ordinal contract.

products.name: Auto Loader (the cloudFiles Structured Streaming source)
products.what_a_senior_person_uses_it_for: Incremental ingest of the SAP landing zone with exactly-once guarantees backed by a RocksDB key-value store in the checkpoint location. Senior work is the schema contract: cloudFiles.schemaLocation, cloudFiles.schemaEvolutionMode (addNewColumns is the default when no schema is provided, but none is the default when a schema is provided), cloudFiles.schemaHints, cloudFiles.inferColumnTypes, and the _rescued_data column that silently absorbs type mismatches, case mismatches and unknown columns. Also knowing Auto Loader gives no ordering guarantee in either directory listing or file notification mode, which matters when ODQ change packets for one sales order land out of order.

products.name: Unity Catalog external locations, storage credentials and volumes
products.what_a_senior_person_uses_it_for: Governing the same ADLS Gen2 paths ADF writes to. A storage credential wraps an access connector for Azure Databricks managed identity; an external location binds it to an abfss:// path; CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE and CREATE EXTERNAL VOLUME are separate grants from CREATE MANAGED LOCATION. Senior gotchas: the storage account must have a hierarchical namespace, containers with immutability (WORM) policies cannot be external locations because Unity Catalog requires DELETE permissions, and file events need Storage Queue Data Contributor plus, for automatic setup, Storage Account Contributor and EventGrid EventSubscription Contributor.

products.name: COPY INTO (Delta)
products.what_a_senior_person_uses_it_for: Bounded, retryable, idempotent backfills of SAP history where Auto Loader's streaming state is unwanted. Files in the source location that have already been loaded are skipped, and Databricks states this is true even if the files have been modified since they were loaded. Senior work is the two COPY_OPTIONS that change everything: force (boolean, default false, disables idempotency) and mergeSchema (boolean, default false). Also VALIDATE [ALL | num_rows ROWS] to prove parseability, schema match and nullability and check constraints before writing, and knowing concurrent invocations succeed only on distinct sets of input files.

products.name: External tables
products.what_a_senior_person_uses_it_for: A read-only, DML-free window over the SAP landing zone for reconciliation and audit, not for serving. Senior facts: AUTO_REFRESH rides cloud storage event notifications (Azure Event Grid), automated refreshes are not supported for Delta Lake external tables because event ordering is inconsistent, partitions are either automatic via expressions parsing METADATA$FILENAME or user-defined via ALTER EXTERNAL TABLE ADD PARTITION, storage versioning is not supported, and materialized views over external tables must be refreshed after the external table metadata changes.

products.name: Power BI semantic model, DAX and row-level security
products.what_a_senior_person_uses_it_for: The layer where the number is actually made. Senior work is knowing that CALCULATE's filter arguments overwrite existing filters on the same columns unless wrapped in KEEPFILTERS, that role-playing SAP dates (order, billing, posting, delivery) need either USERELATIONSHIP measures or duplicated date dimensions and that only one relationship between two tables can be active, that RLS restricts data access only for users with Viewer permissions and does not apply to workspace Admin, Member or Contributor, that RLS combined with USERELATIONSHIP may cause unexpected errors, and that under DirectQuery any query or intermediate operation returning more than 1,000,000 rows fails with a 4-minute service-side query timeout.

products.name: TCURR, TCURF, TCURV, TCURN and TCURX
products.what_a_senior_person_uses_it_for: Currency correctness. Amounts of data type CURR are always stored with 2 decimal places on the database and converted for display based on the currency entry in table TCURX; currencies with a different number of fractional digits must be entered in TCURX where that number is defined explicitly. SAP's documentation also states that the Ratio (from) and Ratio (to) fields in TCURR are not used anymore and that this information is now maintained in TCURF. A senior engineer replicates TCURR, TCURF, TCURV, TCURN and TCURX into the warehouse as first-class tables and treats the TCURX shift as a physical rescale, not a formatting concern.

products.name: T006 unit-of-measure tables, transaction CUNI and ABAP CDS UNIT_CONVERSION
products.what_a_senior_person_uses_it_for: Quantity correctness. Conversion rules live in transaction CUNI and the T006 tables of package SZME, and those tables only contain conversion factors for units with a dimension, meaning material-independent conversions; material-specific conversions (MARM) are a separate problem. SAP states that the precision of a unit conversion depends on the database platform and that due to rounding the result can differ from a conversion performed using a standard function module. Senior work is nominating one conversion authority for the estate and proving warehouse output against SAP output on a fixed sample.

products.name: T002 language table (SPRAS to LAISO) and language-dependent text tables
products.what_a_senior_person_uses_it_for: Text correctness. T002 maps SAP's one-character internal language key SPRAS to the ISO code in LAISO. Single-character SPRAS entries are transferred unchanged and different languages are represented by upper and lower case letters, while two-character entries are case-insensitive; an input that is not defined as T002-LAISO raises the UNKNOWN_LANGUAGE exception. Senior work is deciding whether the warehouse stores SPRAS, LAISO or both, and never letting a text join be language-blind, because a material text table joined without a language predicate multiplies every material row by its translation count.

products.name: Pooled and cluster tables, and their transformation to transparent tables
products.what_a_senior_person_uses_it_for: Knowing what is actually readable. Pooled and cluster tables do not exist with their dictionary definition on the database; only the table pool or table cluster is defined as a special table there. SAP states that on an SAP HANA database only transparent tables should be used because the HANA architecture does not provide optimum support for pooled and cluster tables, and that existing pooled and cluster tables should be transformed to transparent tables. Senior work is inventorying which sources are still classic-database ECC (where cluster content is only reachable through the application layer, hence SLT or an extractor) versus S/4HANA, because the extraction strategy differs completely.

senior_scenarios.title: The revenue figure that was not the ledger: a document-type filter living in DAX instead of the model
senior_scenarios.narrative: Group finance reports full-year net revenue from a Power BI model over a Snowflake FACT_BILLING built by ADF SAP CDC from VBRK and VBRP. Reconciliation against the FI ledger is short by a low single-digit percentage every month, and the gap is not stable. The warehouse table is not wrong. The measure is: Net Revenue = CALCULATE(SUM(FACT_BILLING[NETWR]), FACT_BILLING[FKART] IN {"F2","G2","L2"}). The table holds every billing document type the extractor delivers, including cancellations, pro forma documents and intercompany billing. Three failures compound. First, the filter exists in exactly one measure, so a Databricks notebook, an Excel pivot on the same table, or a second measure written by an analyst all produce a different total from the same governed model. Second, Microsoft documents that if the columns are already in the filter context, the existing filters are overwritten by the new filters unless KEEPFILTERS is used, so a report page slicer set to F2 alone still returns F2 plus G2 plus L2 and the report contradicts its own slicer. Third, cancellation documents net to zero only when paired with the original; excluding the cancellation while keeping the cancelled original inflates revenue in exactly the months a correction was posted, which is why the gap moves. The fix is a document-type dimension carrying an is_revenue_relevant flag applied in the warehouse view, KEEPFILTERS on any measure that must narrow further, and a scheduled reconciliation against FI totals.
senior_scenarios.why_hard: The number is produced by business logic living in a single DAX expression, invisible to column-level lineage, to the warehouse, and to anyone reading the table. Nothing errors. The only symptom is a variance that changes shape month to month, and CALCULATE's documented overwrite semantics mean the report actively misleads about which filter is in force.

senior_scenarios.title: Re-graining the sales fact from header to item: fan-out, a stale Checkpoint Key, and vanished lines
senior_scenarios.narrative: The sales fact is one row per sales document sourced from VBAK, and the business now needs material and plant analysis, so the fact is re-grained to VBAP at (MANDT, VBELN, POSNR). Three things break in the same release and only one of them raises an error. The visible break is fan-out: header-level amounts carried down (header freight and discount conditions, header net value) now sum to the header value multiplied by the line count, and any COUNTROWS measure that meant orders now counts lines, so it must become a distinct count of the document number while the header attributes become a degenerate dimension rather than columns that summarise by default. The invisible break is upstream. The Key columns property must move from ["MANDT","VBELN"] to ["MANDT","VBELN","POSNR"], because Microsoft requires Key columns for both incremental run modes. If the Checkpoint Key is left unchanged, the data flow resumes an existing change-capture process whose state was built under the old key, and the merge collapses arriving change packets to one surviving row per document, silently deleting line items. The second invisible break is that item-level suppression fields, the rejection reason and the deletion indicator, were never extracted, so cancelled lines count as revenue. Recovery needs a new Checkpoint Key, a full reinitialisation, and a reset of the old ODQ subscription in transaction ODQMON, which Data Factory cannot do.
senior_scenarios.why_hard: The grain change, the delta-state key change and the semantic suppression fields sit in three separate systems (Power BI, ADF plus the SAP operational delta queue, and the extractor definition) that must change in one coordinated release. A stale Checkpoint Key produces a pipeline that succeeds, reports rows written, and quietly loses lines. There is no rollback inside ADF: Microsoft states you cannot reset or delete ODQ subscriptions in Data Factory and must use transaction ODQMON.

senior_scenarios.title: TCURX and the currency that was wrong by a factor of one hundred
senior_scenarios.narrative: A margin dashboard shows one legal entity generating implausible profit. The pipeline is clean, the join keys are correct, and nothing failed. SAP stores amount fields of type CURR with two decimal places on the database and converts them for display using TCURX, and currencies whose fractional digit count differs from two must be maintained there explicitly. The extract landed the raw database value into a Snowflake NUMBER column. For a zero-decimal currency the stored integer is one hundred times the true amount, and a warehouse that never joined TCURX has no way to know. The error survives every check a competent team runs: row counts match, referential integrity holds, the delta subscription is healthy, and the number is positive, plausibly sized within its own column, and consistent run to run. It surfaces only when a second affected currency is aggregated alongside a two-decimal currency and someone senior notices the group total does not move the way the entity totals imply. Compounding it, the exchange rate lookup was built on TCURR's ratio fields, which SAP documents as not used anymore with that information now maintained in TCURF, so the applied rate was the raw quotation without its conversion factor. The correction is to replicate TCURR, TCURF, TCURV, TCURN and TCURX as governed tables, apply the TCURX shift as a physical rescale in the silver layer, and reconcile a fixed document sample against SAP output.
senior_scenarios.why_hard: The wrong number is a well-formed decimal in a well-typed column with correct lineage and a passing pipeline. Both defects, the TCURX decimal shift and the TCURF conversion factor, are properties of SAP configuration tables that most extraction designs never bring into scope, because nobody lists a configuration table as a dependency of a revenue fact.
named_tools: Azure Data Factory SAP CDC connector

silent_failures.failure: Two parameterised SAP CDC data flows share a Checkpoint Key, so the status information of one change-capture process overwrites the other's.
silent_failures.why_invisible: Both pipelines report success. Each run returns a plausible, non-empty delta, because the queue hands back whatever has accumulated since the last confirmed pointer, whoever set it. The affected source simply misses a subset of changes on a subset of runs. Row counts never go to zero, no exception is thrown, and the loss is proportional to how often the two flows interleave, so it reads as ordinary business variance.
silent_failures.what_evidence_would_catch_it: A daily reconciliation that counts source rows in SAP for a bounded key range (one company code and one fiscal year, selected with the same selection-option filter used in the source partitioning scheme) against the warehouse count for the same range, asserting equality rather than similarity. Independently, assert that the number of distinct Checkpoint Key values in use equals the number of distinct parameter sets, and alert on any unexpected subscription count in ODQMON.
silent_failures.doc_reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/connector-sap-change-data-capture and https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/sap-change-data-capture-advanced-topics

silent_failures.failure: Auto Loader routes SAP columns into the _rescued_data column instead of failing, because of a type mismatch, a case mismatch, or a column missing from the pinned schema.
silent_failures.why_invisible: The stream keeps running and the target table keeps growing. The affected column is simply null for the affected rows, and a SUM over a column that is null for a tenth of rows returns a smaller number, not an error. Databricks documents that when used together with rescuedDataColumn, data type mismatches do not cause records to be dropped in DROPMALFORMED mode or throw an error in FAILFAST mode, so the two settings an engineer would reach for to make this loud do not make it loud.
silent_failures.what_evidence_would_catch_it: A hard assertion after every micro-batch that the count of rows where _rescued_data is not null equals zero, failing the job rather than logging. Plus a per-column null-rate baseline compared run over run, because a rescued column presents as a null-rate step change on a specific date.
silent_failures.doc_reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/ingestion/cloud-object-storage/auto-loader/schema

silent_failures.failure: A re-run or corrected SAP extract is skipped because the loader has already seen the filename, or is double-loaded because someone set force to get past it.
silent_failures.why_invisible: Snowpipe stores the path and name of each loaded file and prevents loading files with the same name even if they were later modified and have a different eTag. Databricks COPY INTO skips files already loaded even if they have been modified since. A corrected extract republished under the same name therefore produces a load that reports success and changes nothing. The mirror failure is the engineer who reaches for FORCE = TRUE in Snowflake or force in Databricks to unstick it and duplicates every row in the file. Both outcomes are a completed job with a green status.
silent_failures.what_evidence_would_catch_it: Immutable, content-addressed or run-stamped filenames as an enforced contract, checked by asserting no filename is ever reused. Then a post-load assertion comparing rows written in the batch to the growth in distinct business keys in the target, so a duplicate load shows as a key count that did not grow. The check must be independent of vendor load metadata, since Snowpipe history is kept for 14 days and COPY INTO load status becomes uncertain after 64 days.
silent_failures.doc_reference: https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/data-load-snowpipe-intro, https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/sql/copy-into-table, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/sql/language-manual/delta-copy-into

silent_failures.failure: A text join omits the language key, multiplying every fact or dimension row by its translation count.
silent_failures.why_invisible: In a dimension the effect is a duplicated key that a modeller then covers with a DISTINCT, hiding it. In a fact it is a clean multiplication: every measure scales by the same factor, so ratios, percentages, margin percentages and period-over-period growth all remain correct. Only absolute values are wrong, and wrong by a consistent integer factor that reads as a units or scaling issue rather than a join defect. SAP's one-character SPRAS also carries case significance, since different languages are represented by upper and lower case letters, so a naive uppercase normalisation silently selects the wrong language rather than none.
silent_failures.what_evidence_would_catch_it: A grain assertion on every dimension load: COUNT(*) must equal the count of distinct business keys, failing the job when it does not. A row-count invariant on the fact after every join step, asserting the count is unchanged by any join intended as a lookup. And a validation of SPRAS values against T002-LAISO, failing on any value not present there.
silent_failures.doc_reference: https://help.sap.com/docs/ABAP_PLATFORM_NEW/468a97775123488ab3345a0c48cadd8f/91f21f176f4d1014b6dd926db0e91070.html and https://help.sap.com/doc/saphelp_nw73ehp1/7.31.19/en-US/4a/547e986a8a1cd4e10000000a421937/content.htm

silent_failures.failure: The client field (MANDT) is dropped or assumed constant, so two clients are unioned into one number.
silent_failures.why_invisible: The client field is genuinely constant in most estates most of the time, which is why teams drop it. When a second client appears (a training client refreshed from production, an acquisition landed in the same system, an SLT configuration pointed at a different client), documents with identical document numbers collide on a compound key that no longer includes the client. Depending on merge logic the result is either a silent overwrite, one client's rows replacing the other's with the count unchanged, or a doubled total. Neither raises a constraint violation, because the constraint was defined on the truncated key.
silent_failures.what_evidence_would_catch_it: Keep MANDT in the physical key everywhere, including in the ADF Key columns array, and assert the count of distinct MANDT values equals the expected value on every load. Microsoft's own documentation shows the VBAP key definition written both ways, with and without the client field, which is precisely where the ambiguity enters a design.
silent_failures.doc_reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/sap-change-data-capture-advanced-topics

silent_failures.failure: Out-of-order change packets apply a stale update over a newer one, or a late delete removes a row that was legitimately recreated.
silent_failures.why_invisible: Databricks states Auto Loader does not guarantee the order in which files are discovered or processed, regardless of whether directory listing or file notification mode is used. Snowflake states that while Snowpipe generally loads older files first, there is no guarantee files load in the order they were staged. Microsoft states an ODP change extract can contain multiple changes to the same key and that it is important to respect the order of changes. The merged row is well-formed and internally consistent; it is just an earlier version of the truth. No orphan, no null, no constraint breach. Users report it as 'the report is behind', not as a defect.
silent_failures.what_evidence_would_catch_it: Carry the ODP change indicator or a source change timestamp into the merge predicate and apply an update only when the incoming version is newer, then assert the count of rejected stale updates is non-zero over time, because a permanent zero means the guard is not wired up. For Lakeflow pipelines using AUTO CDC, set pipelines.cdc.tombstoneGCThresholdInSeconds above the maximum expected arrival delay, since the default retention is two days.
silent_failures.doc_reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/ingestion/cloud-object-storage/auto-loader/ and https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/data-load-snowpipe-intro and https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/connector-sap-change-data-capture

silent_failures.failure: A Power BI figure differs from the same figure computed in Snowflake or Databricks because RLS, an inactive relationship, or a DirectQuery limit is silently changing the population.
silent_failures.why_invisible: Three mechanisms, one symptom. RLS only restricts data access for users with Viewer permissions and does not apply to workspace Admin, Member or Contributor roles, so the engineer validating the model sees the unfiltered number and the business sees the filtered one, and both are 'the report'. A role-playing SAP date whose relationship is inactive means the measure aggregates on the active date (say billing date) while the page title says posting date, and only one relationship between two tables can be active. And under DirectQuery, any query or intermediate operation returning more than 1,000,000 rows fails, with a 4-minute per-query service timeout, so a visual that worked degrades as data grows.
silent_failures.what_evidence_would_catch_it: A published reconciliation that runs the identical aggregation three ways for a fixed period and entity: the DAX measure via a DAX query against the published model, a direct SQL query against the warehouse table, and the SAP standard report total. Assert all three agree to the cent, scheduled and failing loudly. Validate RLS knowing that Test as role uses your own identity for dynamic RLS and does not work for DirectQuery models with SSO enabled, so the only real proof is signing in as an actual Viewer.
silent_failures.doc_reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/security/service-admin-row-level-security, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/desktop-directquery-about, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dax/calculate-function-dax

silent_failures.failure: A decimal is quietly rescaled or de-precisioned somewhere between SAP, Parquet, the warehouse type and the semantic model.
silent_failures.why_invisible: Every layer has a legitimate default that is not SAP's. Snowflake's NUMBER default is NUMBER(38,0), maximum precision 38 and maximum scale 37, and Snowflake documents that converting a high-scale NUMBER to DOUBLE and back permanently loses precision, and that floating point operations can have small rounding errors in the least significant digits which can compound through aggregates such as SUM or AVG over large datasets. Auto Loader chooses the widest type when a column has different data types in two Parquet files, and when schema hints are supplied a mismatch is rescued rather than raised. SAP states that unit conversion precision depends on the database platform and that rounding can make the result differ from a standard function module. None of these produce an error; they produce a total that is close.
silent_failures.what_evidence_would_catch_it: Pin explicit DECIMAL precision and scale end to end rather than inferring, and run a penny-level reconciliation: for a fixed document set, assert the warehouse sum equals the SAP report total exactly, not within a tolerance. A tolerance-based check is exactly what lets this class of defect live for years.
silent_failures.doc_reference: https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/data-types-numeric, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/ingestion/cloud-object-storage/auto-loader/schema, https://help.sap.com/doc/abapdocu_752_index_htm/7.52/en-US/abencds_f1_conv_func_unit_curr.htm

silent_failures.failure: The SAP CDC staging folder in ADLS Gen2 is treated as the bronze layer and read by another pipeline.
silent_failures.why_invisible: It works. The files are there, they parse, and a second copy activity or mapping data flow reading them produces data that looks correct today. Microsoft explicitly designates that folder internal storage of the SAP CDC connector and warns that implementation details such as the file format used for the staging data might change as the runtime is optimised. The failure arrives on a service-side change nobody in the estate scheduled, at which point a downstream pipeline that has not been touched in a year begins producing wrong or unparseable output.
silent_failures.what_evidence_would_catch_it: A storage-level control rather than a data check: RBAC that grants no read on the staging container to any identity other than the SAP CDC runtime, plus a repository grep across the ADF and Databricks source asserting that no dataset, notebook, external location or external volume path resolves to the staging container. That grep returning empty is the done-check.
silent_failures.doc_reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/connector-sap-change-data-capture

silent_failures.failure: An Iceberg or lakehouse table is written by a second engine that the first engine's governance model does not expect.
silent_failures.why_invisible: Both engines report success on their own writes. Snowflake documents that third-party clients cannot append to, delete from, or upsert data to Iceberg tables that use Snowflake as the catalog, while catalog-linked databases against Unity Catalog support both read and write by default, so the direction of permitted writes depends on which catalog owns the table, which is invisible from the table name. Unity Catalog also does not govern reads and writes performed directly against cloud object storage from external systems, so a process holding storage-account credentials can write files that the catalog never sees. The result is a table whose row count and history look coherent to each engine separately.
silent_failures.what_evidence_would_catch_it: Name a single writing engine per table and prove it: for Snowflake-managed Iceberg tables, mark the external volume or the storage credential read-only for every other principal; for Unity Catalog paths, verify with the storage credential 'Limit to read-only use' setting and with cloud-native IAM aligned to the Unity Catalog grants. Then reconcile the catalog's row count against a direct file scan of the underlying path on a schedule; a divergence proves an ungoverned writer.
silent_failures.doc_reference: https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/tables-iceberg, https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/tables-iceberg-configure-catalog-integration-rest-unity, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/volumes/

checked.area: Where SAP data lands and becomes a reported number: ADF SAP CDC staging into ADLS Gen2, landing into Snowflake or Databricks, SAP-specific physical and semantic modelling (currency, unit, language, client), and the Power BI semantic layer where a measure diverges from the warehouse table.
corrections_to_my_facts: HEADLINE REFUTATION, the currency scenario is inverted and cannot happen as narrated. The research says that for a zero-decimal currency 'the stored integer is one hundred times the true amount' and that the symptom is 'one legal entity generating implausible profit'. The shift runs the other way. SAP's ABAP CDS documentation for CURRENCY_CONVERSION defines decimal_shift (default 'X') as: the value passed is multiplied by 10 to the power of two minus the number of decimal places of the source currency before it is converted, with the decimal places read from column CURRDEC of TCURX. For a zero-decimal currency (JPY, KRW, VND) that is a multiplication by 100 applied to the stored value, which means the raw database value is one hundred times SMALLER than the true amount. A warehouse that never joins TCURX therefore UNDERSTATES those entities by 100x: margin collapses, revenue looks trivial, nobody reports implausible profit. The direction reverses for three-decimal currencies (KWD, BHD, TND), where the raw value is ten times LARGER than the true amount. Print the scenario as written and any SAP-literate reader stops trusting the booklet on page one. Source: https://help.sap.com/doc/abapdocu_752_index_htm/7.52/en-US/abencds_f1_conv_func_unit_curr.htm

IMPLAUSIBLE AS NARRATED, all three scenarios extract raw SAP application tables with no SLT anywhere in the story: FACT_BILLING 'built by ADF SAP CDC from VBRK and VBRP', a sales fact 'sourced from VBAK' re-grained to VBAP, and a currency scenario on the same base. The research's own correction number 4 says direct table extraction is not on Microsoft's list, and the architecture page confirms it: the ODP source types are SAP extractors, ABAP CDS views, InfoProviders and InfoObjects, and 'SAP application tables, when you use an SAP LT replication server (SLT) as a proxy'. A principal-level reader will notice the contradiction between the correction and the scenarios in the same document. Fix: name the SLT path explicitly (ODP context SLT~<Queue Alias>, alias taken from Administration Data in the SLT cockpit, transaction LTRC), or source a CDS view or an SD billing extractor and stop naming the transparent table. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/sap-change-data-capture-introduction-architecture and https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/sap-change-data-capture-advanced-topics

MECHANIC DESCRIBED WRONGLY, the re-graining scenario blames the Checkpoint Key for a failure the Key columns property causes. Microsoft documents exactly one consequence of a non-unique Checkpoint Key: 'It is therefore important to use a unique Checkpoint Key for each source. Otherwise status information of one source will be overwritten by another source.' That is a corrupted delta pointer, not a merge that collapses line items. The collapse-to-one-row-per-document failure comes from the Key columns array, because 'an extract of change data from ODP can contain multiple changes to the same key' and both incremental run modes 'require to specify the keys of the ODP source object in the Key columns property'. A header-only key makes every item change of a document a competing version of one row. Separately, re-graining changes the ODP source object itself, so there is no documented mechanism by which the old checkpoint state 'resumes' against the new object and issues deletes for lines it never saw. Split this into two failure modes or a senior reader will discount both. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/connector-sap-change-data-capture

The DirectQuery one million row limit is not the hard wall the research implies. The page states: 'One million row intermediate result limit. Any query (or intermediate operation) that returns more than 1,000,000 rows fails. Premium capacities can raise this limit' via the Max Intermediate Row Set Count setting. For an estate on Premium or Fabric capacity the number is a tunable, and a booklet that presents it as fixed will send someone rearchitecting a model when a capacity setting was the answer. The 4-minute timeout claim IS correct and verbatim: 'The service enforces a 4-minute timeout per query.' Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/desktop-directquery-about

The Fabric alternatives are quoted without their availability status, which is the whole point of citing them in August 2026. Microsoft's page marks only ONE as shipped: 'Mirroring for SAP Datasphere in Fabric (Generally Available)'. 'SAP Business Data Cloud Connect for Microsoft Fabric' carries the parenthetical '(Announced at Microsoft Ignite 2025, available later this year)', which is stale doc text relative to today and is not a GA statement. 'Copy Job in Fabric for SAP with ABAP Add-on' is marked '(publicly available at Microsoft Build 2026)'. Presenting all four as live options misstates the migration menu. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/sap-change-data-capture-introduction-architecture

Scenario 1's KEEPFILTERS argument is only true under a precondition the narrative never states. CALCULATE overwrites existing filters on the SAME columns. If the page slicer sits on FACT_BILLING[FKART], the report does contradict its own slicer. If the slicer sits on a separate document-type dimension (which is what the scenario's own fix recommends building), the filter is not overwritten and the contradiction disappears. State the precondition, because a principal reader will test it and find the counterexample in thirty seconds. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dax/calculate-function-dax (behaviour restated on the RLS and DirectQuery pages I opened)

Snowflake V2 typing claim is half the sentence. Microsoft's version 1.0 release notes say BOTH 'The NUMBER type, as defined in Snowflake, will be displayed as a string in Lookup activity' AND, three bullets later, 'NUMBER (p,0) is read as Decimal data type.' Writing only the first half tells engineers integer-scale columns arrive as strings, which is wrong. Everything else in that correction is verbatim and survives: V1 'is at removal stage', version 1.0 lacks script parameters and multi-statement Script activity, TIMESTAMP_LTZ/NTZ/TZ read as DateTimeOffset, version 1.1 restores both and adds treatDecimalAsString (default false, version 1.1 only). Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/connector-snowflake

The Iceberg unsupported list is incomplete and the streams claim needs its exception. Snowflake lists for ALL Iceberg tables: Fail-safe, hybrid tables, Snowflake encryption, Snowflake schema evolution, temporary and transient tables, and tagging via ASSOCIATE_SEMANTIC_CATEGORY_TAGS. The externally-managed-only restrictions are cloning, clustering, standard and append-only streams (insert-only streams ARE supported), and replication of Iceberg tables, external volumes or catalog integrations. Saying 'standard streams work only on Snowflake-managed ones' without the insert-only carve-out removes a CDC pattern that is actually available. Source: https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/tables-iceberg

Cite the tombstone default from the right page or a reviewer will call it invented. 'The default retention is two days' IS correct and verbatim, but it appears on the Auto Loader overview page, not on the AUTO CDC reference the research implies: the AUTO CDC INTO page names pipelines.cdc.tombstoneGCThresholdInSeconds and its purpose but states no default, and the pipeline properties reference does not list the property at all. Sources: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/ingestion/cloud-object-storage/auto-loader/ (default), https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/ldp/developer/ldp-sql-ref-apply-changes-into (no default stated)

UNVERIFIED, do not print as fact: the claim that a language value not defined as T002-LAISO 'raises the UNKNOWN_LANGUAGE exception'. help.sap.com's modern docs pages are JavaScript-rendered and served me an empty shell, so I could not open the cited page. What I could find describes the opposite behaviour for the output direction of the ISOLA conversion exit: an unconvertible value returns OUTPUT = INPUT(1), a silent truncation to one character with no error message. The load-bearing part of the failure (SPRAS is one character and case-significant, T002 maps it to LAISO, a language-blind text join multiplies rows) stands; the exception name does not, and it is the kind of detail a staff engineer checks.

Trim the currency table list to what SAP actually documents together. The ABAP CDS page says currency conversion rules come from 'database tables TCUR... of package SFIB' and are edited with transaction OB08, without enumerating five tables; unit conversion comes from transaction CUNI and 'the database tables T006... of the package SZME'. The TCURR-to-TCURF point is real and documented ('Fields Ratio (from) and Ratio (to) in table TCURR are not used any longer. This information is now maintained in table TCURF'), but that page is on the JS-rendered part of help.sap.com that I could not open directly, so it reached me through search results only, single-sourced. Recommend: name TCURR, TCURF and TCURX as load-bearing, name package SFIB and transaction OB08, and treat TCURV and TCURN as secondary rather than asserting a five-table canon.

On your own facts, two additions and one caveat. (a) State the SAP CDC capability as mapping data flow, SOURCE ONLY: the supported capabilities table reads 'Mapping data flow (source/-)'. There is no copy activity SAP CDC source and no SAP CDC sink, which kills the 'we will just use a copy activity' shortcut in design review. (b) Your ODP source list should carry the SLT proviso for application tables, and your ODP context list should include HANA (SAP HANA Information Views) alongside ABAP_CDS, BW, SAPI, SLT~<Queue Alias>, ODP_SELF and RANDOM. (c) Everything else you listed about ADF Git, publish branches, the CDC connector, the staging linked service, the Checkpoint Key, ODQMON and unsupported hierarchies checked out verbatim against the pages I opened. Your SAP Integration Suite capability list I did NOT re-verify this session (SAP's Feature Scope Description is on the JS-rendered part of help.sap.com); treat it as carried over, not as confirmed by this pass. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/connector-sap-change-data-capture

Minor sourcing point on the Snowpipe eTag phrasing. The Snowpipe overview page I opened says load history is kept 'in the metadata of the pipe for 14 days' versus 'the metadata of the target table for 64 days' for COPY, that Snowpipe tracks 'path (i.e. prefix) and name of each loaded file, and prevents loading files with the same name even if they were later modified', that loads are 'combined or split into a single or multiple transactions', and that 'while Snowpipe generally loads older files first, there is no guarantee that files are loaded in the same order they are staged'. The explicit 'different eTag' wording was not on that page; attribute it to the COPY INTO <table> reference or drop it. Source: https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/data-load-snowpipe-intro

products.name: SAP CDC connector (mapping data flow source, source only)
products.what_a_senior_person_uses_it_for: Establishing and owning ODQ delta subscriptions against ECC, S/4HANA, BW, BW/4HANA and SLT, now under a live strategic caveat: Microsoft's architecture page carries an Important notice that a recent update of SAP Note 3255746 announces a security patch blocking incoming calls to the ODP RFC API from third-party clients including this connector. The senior work is not building the data flow. It is governing the Checkpoint Key namespace across a parameterised fleet, choosing Key columns per ODP object (mandatory for both fullAndIncrementalLoad and incrementalLoad), designing the JSON source partitioning scheme (arrays of {fieldName, sign, option, low, high}, SAP internal format with leading zeroes and YYYYMMDD dates, non-overlapping because Azure Data Factory performs no checks on these conditions), and knowing that debug runs use a different subscriber process value than triggered runs and that value's lifetime is limited to the browser UI session, so change-capture stability can only be proven with published, triggered runs. Capability table reads 'Mapping data flow (source/-)': no copy activity source, no sink.

products.name: Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2, as SAP CDC staging and separately as the governed landing zone
products.what_a_senior_person_uses_it_for: Two physically separate containers that juniors conflate. Container one is the SAP CDC staging folder, which Microsoft says 'should be considered an internal storage of the SAP CDC connector', whose file format 'might change', which cannot use a self-hosted integration runtime, and which Microsoft recommends not using 'for other purposes, e.g. as a source for other copy activities or mapping data flows'. Container two is the actual landing zone written by the data flow sink, laid out with Hive-style partitioning, sized for the downstream reader, and registered to a Unity Catalog external location or a Snowflake external volume. Senior work is enforcing that separation in the ARM template and in storage RBAC, not in a wiki page.

products.name: Apache Iceberg tables and external volumes
products.what_a_senior_person_uses_it_for: Deciding, per table, between a Snowflake-managed Iceberg table (full platform support, but 'third-party clients can't append to, delete from, or upsert data to Iceberg tables that use Snowflake as the catalog') and an externally managed one via catalog integration. The external volume is a named, account-level object binding Snowflake to the ADLS Gen2 path. Senior work is knowing the unsupported list for ALL Iceberg tables (Fail-safe, hybrid tables, Snowflake encryption, Snowflake schema evolution, temporary and transient tables, ASSOCIATE_SEMANTIC_CATEGORY_TAGS tagging) and the externally-managed-only restrictions (cloning, clustering, standard and append-only streams with insert-only streams still supported, and replication), because that combination quietly removes several recovery and CDC patterns.

products.name: Catalog integration for Unity Catalog (Iceberg REST) and catalog-linked databases
products.what_a_senior_person_uses_it_for: Running Snowflake and Databricks over one physical copy of the SAP facts instead of two divergent copies. Catalog-linked databases against Unity Catalog support both read and write, authenticated by OAuth with a Databricks service principal or by a personal access token (legacy, inheriting the creating user's privileges), using vended credentials or an external volume, with EXTERNAL USE SCHEMA required on the Databricks side only for the vended-credentials path and external data access enabled at the metastore first. Senior work is deciding who owns the single write path, because two engines writing one Iceberg table is where the reconciliation story dies.

products.name: Snowpipe and COPY INTO <table>
products.what_a_senior_person_uses_it_for: Choosing between them on load-history semantics rather than latency marketing. Snowpipe keeps load history in the pipe metadata for 14 days and tracks path and name of each loaded file, preventing a reload of the same name even if the file was later modified; COPY keeps load metadata in the target table for 64 days. Snowpipe combines or splits a load into one or multiple transactions and, while it generally loads older files first, gives no ordering guarantee. Senior work is designing filenames so a corrected SAP extract is a new name rather than an overwrite, reserving FORCE = TRUE for a deliberate, logged replay, and using MATCH_BY_COLUMN_NAME so Parquet lands without an ordinal contract.

products.name: Auto Loader (the cloudFiles Structured Streaming source)
products.what_a_senior_person_uses_it_for: Incremental ingest of the SAP landing zone, with file metadata persisted in a RocksDB key-value store in the checkpoint location that 'ensures that data is processed exactly once'. Senior work is the schema contract: cloudFiles.schemaLocation, cloudFiles.schemaEvolutionMode (addNewColumns is the default when no schema is provided, none when a schema is provided, and addNewColumns is not allowed with a provided schema though it works as a schema hint), cloudFiles.schemaHints, cloudFiles.inferColumnTypes, and the _rescued_data column that absorbs missing columns, type mismatches and case mismatches. Also that inference samples the first 50 GB or 1000 files, that Auto Loader picks the widest type when a column differs across two Parquet files, and that it 'does not guarantee the order in which files are discovered or processed, regardless of whether you use directory listing or file notification mode'.

products.name: Unity Catalog external locations, storage credentials and volumes
products.what_a_senior_person_uses_it_for: Governing the same ADLS Gen2 paths ADF writes to. A storage credential wraps an access connector for Azure Databricks managed identity; an external location binds it to an abfss:// path; CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE and CREATE EXTERNAL VOLUME are separate grants from CREATE MANAGED LOCATION. Senior gotchas, all verbatim in the docs: the storage account must have a hierarchical namespace; 'You cannot use Azure storage containers with immutability (WORM - Write Once, Read Many) policies enabled as external locations. Unity Catalog requires DELETE permissions on storage containers, which immutability policies prevent'; file events need Storage Queue Data Contributor, plus Storage Account Contributor and EventGrid EventSubscription Contributor for automatic setup; and 'Limit to read-only use' exists on both the storage credential and the external location.

products.name: COPY INTO (Delta)
products.what_a_senior_person_uses_it_for: Bounded, retryable, idempotent backfills of SAP history where Auto Loader's streaming state is unwanted. 'Files in the source location that have already been loaded are skipped. This is true even if the files have been modified since they were loaded.' Senior work is the two COPY_OPTIONS that change everything: force (boolean, default false, 'idempotency is disabled and files are loaded regardless of whether they've been loaded before') and mergeSchema (boolean, default false). Also VALIDATE [ALL | num_rows ROWS], which checks parseability, schema match or needed evolution, and nullability and check constraints without writing, and knowing concurrent invocations succeed only on distinct sets of input files or you get a transaction conflict.

products.name: External tables
products.what_a_senior_person_uses_it_for: A read-only, DML-free window over the SAP landing zone for reconciliation and audit, not for serving. Senior facts: AUTO_REFRESH rides cloud storage event notifications; automated refreshes are not supported for Delta Lake external tables 'because the ordering of event notifications triggered by Data Definition Language (DDL) operations in cloud storage isn't guaranteed'; partitions are either expression-based over METADATA$FILENAME or user-defined via PARTITION_TYPE = USER_SPECIFIED plus ALTER EXTERNAL TABLE ADD PARTITION; storage versioning is not supported; and materialized views over external tables need the external table's file-level metadata refreshed to reflect the current file set.

products.name: Power BI semantic model, DAX and row-level security
products.what_a_senior_person_uses_it_for: The layer where the number is actually made. Senior work is knowing that CALCULATE's filter arguments overwrite existing filters on the same columns unless wrapped in KEEPFILTERS; that role-playing SAP dates (order, billing, posting, delivery) need USERELATIONSHIP measures or duplicated date dimensions because only one relationship between two tables can be active; that 'RLS only restricts data access for users with Viewer permissions. It doesn't apply to workspace Admin, Member, or Contributor roles'; that 'With RLS enabled, using the USERELATIONSHIP() function in DAX queries and measures might cause unexpected errors'; and that under DirectQuery any query or intermediate operation returning more than 1,000,000 rows fails (raisable on Premium via Max Intermediate Row Set Count) under a 4-minute service-side per-query timeout.

products.name: TCURR, TCURF and TCURX (the TCUR* tables of package SFIB, transaction OB08)
products.what_a_senior_person_uses_it_for: Currency correctness, in the correct direction. Amounts of data type CURR are stored on the database with two decimal places and shifted for the currency's real precision using column CURRDEC of TCURX: SAP's CURRENCY_CONVERSION decimal_shift multiplies the passed value by 10 to the power of (2 minus the source currency's decimal places), so a zero-decimal currency's raw stored value is 100x SMALLER than the true amount and a three-decimal currency's is 10x larger. Conversion rules live in the TCUR* tables of package SFIB, edited with transaction OB08, and the Ratio (from) and Ratio (to) fields of TCURR are documented as no longer used, with that information maintained in TCURF. A senior engineer replicates these as first-class governed tables and treats the TCURX shift as a physical rescale, not a formatting concern.

products.name: T006 unit-of-measure tables, transaction CUNI and ABAP CDS UNIT_CONVERSION
products.what_a_senior_person_uses_it_for: Quantity correctness. Conversion rules are 'client-specific rules saved in transaction CUNI and in the database tables T006... of the package SZME', which cover material-independent conversions only; material-specific conversions (MARM) are a separate problem. SAP states that 'the precision of the result of the unit conversion depends on the database platform', that the highest precision is on databases supporting decimal floating point, and that 'due to rounding, the result can be different from a unit conversion performed using ABAP methods, such as a standard function module'. Senior work is nominating one conversion authority for the estate and proving warehouse output against SAP output on a fixed sample.

products.name: T002 language table (SPRAS to LAISO) and language-dependent text tables
products.what_a_senior_person_uses_it_for: Text correctness. T002 maps SAP's one-character internal language key SPRAS to the two-character code in LAISO, and SPRAS is case-significant, so upper and lower case of the same letter are different languages and a naive uppercase normalisation selects the wrong language rather than none. Senior work is deciding whether the warehouse stores SPRAS, LAISO or both, and never letting a text join be language-blind, because a material text table joined without a language predicate multiplies every material row by its translation count. Confidence is unsure rather than certain because help.sap.com's modern pages are JavaScript-rendered and did not serve content to my fetcher, so the exception-name detail (UNKNOWN_LANGUAGE) is not confirmed and should not be printed.

products.name: Pooled and cluster tables, and their transformation to transparent tables
products.what_a_senior_person_uses_it_for: Knowing what is actually readable: pooled and cluster tables do not exist with their dictionary definition on the database, only the pool or cluster does, so on HANA the guidance is to use transparent tables and transform existing pooled and cluster tables. Senior work is inventorying which sources are still classic-database ECC (cluster content reachable only through the application layer, hence SLT or an extractor) versus S/4HANA, because the extraction strategy differs completely. senior_scenarios.title: The revenue figure that was not the ledger: a document-type filter living in DAX instead of the model
senior_scenarios.narrative: Group finance reports full-year net revenue from a Power BI model over a Snowflake FACT_BILLING, landed by ADF SAP CDC through an SLT-proxied ODP context (context SLT~<Queue Alias>, alias from Administration Data in transaction LTRC) because billing transparent tables are reachable only with SLT as proxy. Reconciliation against the FI ledger is short by a low single-digit percentage every month, and the gap is not stable. The warehouse table is not wrong. The measure is: Net Revenue = CALCULATE(SUM(FACT_BILLING[NETWR]), FACT_BILLING[FKART] IN {"F2","G2","L2"}). The table holds every billing document type the source delivers, including cancellations, pro forma and intercompany documents. Three failures compound. First, the filter exists in exactly one measure, so a Databricks notebook, an Excel pivot on the same table, or a second measure written by an analyst all produce a different total from the same governed model. Second, Microsoft documents that filter arguments overwrite existing filters on the same columns unless KEEPFILTERS is used, so a page slicer bound to FACT_BILLING[FKART] itself still returns F2 plus G2 plus L2 and the report contradicts its own slicer, while a slicer on a separate document-type dimension does not, which is why the defect appears on some pages and not others. Third, cancellation documents net to zero only when paired with the original, so excluding the cancellation while keeping the cancelled original inflates revenue in exactly the months a correction was posted, which is why the gap moves.
senior_scenarios.why_hard: The number is produced by business logic living in a single DAX expression, invisible to column-level lineage, to the warehouse, and to anyone reading the table. Nothing errors. The only symptom is a variance that changes shape month to month, and CALCULATE's documented overwrite semantics mean the report actively misleads about which filter is in force on precisely the pages where the slicer targets the fact column.
