senior_scenarios.title: Re-graining the sales fact from header to item: fan-out, a header-only Key columns array, and a subscription only SAP can reset
senior_scenarios.narrative: The sales fact is one row per sales document, extracted through an SLT queue over the SAP sales header table, and the business now needs material and plant analysis, so the fact is re-grained to the item table at (MANDT, VBELN, POSNR). Three things break in the same release and only one of them raises an error. The visible break is fan-out: header-level amounts carried down (header freight and discount conditions, header net value) now sum to the header value multiplied by the line count, and any COUNTROWS measure that meant orders now counts lines, so it must become a distinct count of the document number while header attributes become a degenerate dimension rather than columns that summarise by default. The first invisible break is the Key columns array. Microsoft requires the keys of the ODP source object for both incremental run modes, and documents that an ODP change extract can contain multiple changes to the same key, so leaving the array at ["MANDT","VBELN"] makes every item change of a document a competing version of one row and the surviving row is whichever change won. Separately, the Checkpoint Key must be new, because it carries the status of a different change-capture process and Microsoft's rule is one unique key per source. The second invisible break is that item-level suppression fields, the rejection reason and the deletion indicator, were never extracted, so cancelled lines count as revenue.
senior_scenarios.why_hard: The grain change, the ODP key definition and the semantic suppression fields sit in three separate systems (Power BI, ADF plus the SAP operational delta queue, and the extraction definition) that must change in one coordinated release. A wrong Key columns array produces a pipeline that succeeds and reports rows written while silently keeping one version per document. There is no rollback inside ADF: Microsoft's current limitations state 'You can't reset or delete ODQ subscriptions in Data Factory (use transaction ODQMON in the connected SAP system for this purpose).'
named_tools: Azure Data Factory SAP CDC connector

silent_failures.failure: Two parameterised SAP CDC data flows share a Checkpoint Key, so the status information of one change-capture process is overwritten by the other.
silent_failures.why_invisible: Both pipelines report success. Microsoft's documented consequence is precisely that status information of one source is overwritten by another, and the status is what tells the runtime where the last confirmed delta ended, so the affected source misses a subset of changes on a subset of runs. Row counts never go to zero, no exception is thrown, and the loss is proportional to how often the two flows interleave, so it reads as ordinary business variance. Note that a unique ID is generated as Checkpoint Key by default, so this only bites where engineers parameterise one data flow across many sources or pin a static key.
silent_failures.what_evidence_would_catch_it: A daily reconciliation that counts source rows in SAP for a bounded key range (one company code and one fiscal year, selected with the same selection-option filter used in the source partitioning scheme) against the warehouse count for the same range, asserting equality rather than similarity. Independently, assert that the number of distinct Checkpoint Key values in use equals the number of distinct parameter sets, and alert on any unexpected subscription count in ODQMON.
silent_failures.doc_reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/connector-sap-change-data-capture and https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/sap-change-data-capture-advanced-topics

silent_failures.failure: Auto Loader routes SAP columns into the _rescued_data column instead of failing, because of a type mismatch, a case mismatch, or a column missing from the pinned schema.
silent_failures.why_invisible: The stream keeps running and the target table keeps growing. The affected column is simply null for the affected rows, and a SUM over a column that is null for a tenth of rows returns a smaller number, not an error. Databricks documents that when used together with rescuedDataColumn, data type mismatches do not cause records to be dropped in DROPMALFORMED mode or throw an error in FAILFAST mode, so the two settings an engineer would reach for to make this loud do not make it loud. Schema hints make it worse: with a hint, Auto Loader tells the reader to read the column as the hinted type and, on mismatch, rescues the column rather than raising.
silent_failures.what_evidence_would_catch_it: A hard assertion after every micro-batch that the count of rows where _rescued_data is not null equals zero, failing the job rather than logging. Plus a per-column null-rate baseline compared run over run, because a rescued column presents as a null-rate step change on a specific date.
silent_failures.doc_reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/ingestion/cloud-object-storage/auto-loader/schema

silent_failures.failure: A re-run or corrected SAP extract is skipped because the loader has already seen the filename, or is double-loaded because someone disabled idempotency to get past it.
silent_failures.why_invisible: Snowpipe stores the path and name of each loaded file and prevents loading files with the same name even if they were later modified. Databricks COPY INTO skips files already loaded, and states this is true even if the files have been modified since they were loaded. A corrected extract republished under the same name therefore produces a load that reports success and changes nothing. The mirror failure is the engineer who reaches for FORCE = TRUE in Snowflake or force = true in Databricks (default false, 'idempotency is disabled') and duplicates every row in the file. Both outcomes are a completed job with a green status.
silent_failures.what_evidence_would_catch_it: Immutable, content-addressed or run-stamped filenames as an enforced contract, checked by asserting no filename is ever reused. Then a post-load assertion comparing rows written in the batch to the growth in distinct business keys in the target, so a duplicate load shows as a key count that did not grow. The check must be independent of vendor load metadata, since Snowpipe history lives in the pipe metadata for 14 days and COPY load metadata lives in the target table for 64 days.
silent_failures.doc_reference: https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/data-load-snowpipe-intro and https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/sql/language-manual/delta-copy-into

silent_failures.failure: A text join omits the language key, multiplying every fact or dimension row by its translation count.
silent_failures.why_invisible: In a dimension the effect is a duplicated key that a modeller then covers with a DISTINCT, hiding it. In a fact it is a clean multiplication: every measure scales by the same factor, so ratios, percentages, margin percentages and period-over-period growth all remain correct. Only absolute values are wrong, and wrong by a consistent integer factor that reads as a units or scaling issue rather than a join defect. SAP's one-character SPRAS is also case-significant, so a naive uppercase normalisation selects a different language rather than none.
silent_failures.what_evidence_would_catch_it: A grain assertion on every dimension load: COUNT(*) must equal the count of distinct business keys, failing the job when it does not. A row-count invariant on the fact after every join step, asserting the count is unchanged by any join intended as a lookup. And a validation of every language value against the replicated T002 contents, failing on any value not present there. Do not cite a specific ABAP exception name in the booklet: that detail could not be confirmed against an openable vendor page.
silent_failures.doc_reference: SAP T002 / SPRAS-to-LAISO mapping; the specific help.sap.com pages are JavaScript-rendered and did not serve content to my fetcher, so treat this reference as unconfirmed this pass.

silent_failures.failure: The client field (MANDT) is dropped or assumed constant, so two clients are unioned into one number.
silent_failures.why_invisible: The client field is genuinely constant in most estates most of the time, which is why teams drop it. When a second client appears (a training client refreshed from production, an acquisition landed in the same system, an SLT configuration pointed at a different client), documents with identical document numbers collide on a compound key that no longer includes the client. Depending on merge logic the result is either a silent overwrite, one client's rows replacing the other's with the count unchanged, or a doubled total. Neither raises a constraint violation, because the constraint was defined on the truncated key.
silent_failures.what_evidence_would_catch_it: Keep MANDT in the physical key everywhere, including in the ADF Key columns array, and assert the count of distinct MANDT values equals the expected value on every load. Microsoft's own documentation writes the VBAP key definition both ways, as ["VBELN", "POSNR"] 'or ["MANDT","VBELN","POSNR"] in case the client field is taken into account as well', which is precisely where the ambiguity enters a design.
silent_failures.doc_reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/sap-change-data-capture-advanced-topics

silent_failures.failure: Out-of-order change packets apply a stale update over a newer one, or a late delete removes a row that was legitimately recreated.
silent_failures.why_invisible: Databricks states Auto Loader 'does not guarantee the order in which files are discovered or processed, regardless of whether you use directory listing or file notification mode'. Snowflake states that while Snowpipe generally loads older files first, there is no guarantee files load in the order they were staged. Microsoft states an ODP change extract can contain multiple changes to the same key and that it is important to respect the order of changes. The merged row is well-formed and internally consistent; it is just an earlier version of the truth. No orphan, no null, no constraint breach. Users report it as 'the report is behind', not as a defect.
silent_failures.what_evidence_would_catch_it: Carry the ODP change indicator or a source change timestamp into the merge predicate and apply an update only when the incoming version is newer, then assert the count of rejected stale updates is non-zero over time, because a permanent zero means the guard is not wired up. For Lakeflow pipelines using AUTO CDC, set pipelines.cdc.tombstoneGCThresholdInSeconds above the maximum expected delay between event arrival and pipeline execution, since the default retention is two days.
silent_failures.doc_reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/ingestion/cloud-object-storage/auto-loader/ and https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/data-load-snowpipe-intro and https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/connector-sap-change-data-capture

silent_failures.failure: A Power BI figure differs from the same figure computed in Snowflake or Databricks because RLS, an inactive relationship, or a DirectQuery limit is silently changing the population.
silent_failures.why_invisible: Three mechanisms, one symptom. 'RLS only restricts data access for users with Viewer permissions. It doesn't apply to workspace Admin, Member, or Contributor roles', so the engineer validating the model sees the unfiltered number and the business sees the filtered one, and both are 'the report'. A role-playing SAP date whose relationship is inactive means the measure aggregates on the active date while the page title says posting date, and only one relationship between two tables can be active. And under DirectQuery, any query or intermediate operation returning more than 1,000,000 rows fails (Premium capacities can raise this via Max Intermediate Row Set Count) under a 4-minute service-side per-query timeout, so a visual that worked degrades as data grows.
silent_failures.what_evidence_would_catch_it: A published reconciliation that runs the identical aggregation three ways for a fixed period and entity: the DAX measure via a DAX query against the published model, a direct SQL query against the warehouse table, and the SAP standard report total. Assert all three agree to the cent, scheduled and failing loudly. Validate RLS knowing that Test as role uses your own identity for dynamic RLS and 'doesn't work for DirectQuery models with single sign-on (SSO) enabled', so the only real proof is signing in as an actual Viewer.
silent_failures.doc_reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/security/service-admin-row-level-security and https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/desktop-directquery-about

silent_failures.failure: A decimal is quietly rescaled or de-precisioned somewhere between SAP, Parquet, the warehouse type and the semantic model, including the TCURX shift itself.
silent_failures.why_invisible: Every layer has a legitimate default that is not SAP's. SAP stores CURR amounts with two decimals and shifts by 10 to the power of (2 minus the currency's decimal places) from TCURX.CURRDEC, so a zero-decimal currency arrives 100x too small unless the shift is applied. Snowflake's NUMBER default is NUMBER(38,0), maximum precision 38 and maximum scale 37, and Snowflake documents that converting a NUMBER(38,37) to DOUBLE and back loses precision and that errors 'can accumulate, especially when aggregate functions, for example SUM or AVG, process large numbers of rows'. Auto Loader chooses the widest type when a column has different types across two Parquet files, and rescues rather than raises when a schema hint mismatches. SAP states unit conversion precision depends on the database platform. None of these produce an error; they produce a total that is close.
silent_failures.what_evidence_would_catch_it: Pin explicit DECIMAL precision and scale end to end rather than inferring, apply the TCURX shift as a physical rescale in the silver layer, and run a penny-level reconciliation: for a fixed document set, assert the warehouse sum equals the SAP report total exactly, not within a tolerance. A tolerance-based check is exactly what lets this class of defect live for years, and it is what hides a 100x currency shift on a small entity inside a large group total.
silent_failures.doc_reference: https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/data-types-numeric and https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/ingestion/cloud-object-storage/auto-loader/schema and https://help.sap.com/doc/abapdocu_752_index_htm/7.52/en-US/abencds_f1_conv_func_unit_curr.htm

silent_failures.failure: The SAP CDC staging folder in ADLS Gen2 is treated as the bronze layer and read by another pipeline.
silent_failures.why_invisible: It works. The files are there, they parse, and a second copy activity or mapping data flow reading them produces data that looks correct today. Microsoft says the staging folder 'should be considered an internal storage of the SAP CDC connector', that implementation details 'like the file format used for the staging data, might change', and recommends 'not to use the staging folder for other purposes, e.g. as a source for other copy activities or mapping data flows'. The failure arrives on a service-side change nobody in the estate scheduled, at which point a downstream pipeline untouched for a year begins producing wrong or unparseable output.
silent_failures.what_evidence_would_catch_it: A storage-level control rather than a data check: RBAC that grants no read on the staging container to any identity other than the SAP CDC runtime, plus a repository grep across the ADF and Databricks source asserting that no dataset, notebook, external location or external volume path resolves to the staging container. That grep returning empty is the done-check.
silent_failures.doc_reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/connector-sap-change-data-capture

silent_failures.failure: An Iceberg or lakehouse table is written by a second engine that the first engine's governance model does not expect.
silent_failures.why_invisible: Both engines report success on their own writes. Snowflake documents that 'third-party clients can't append to, delete from, or upsert data to Iceberg tables that use Snowflake as the catalog', while catalog-linked databases against Unity Catalog support both read and write, so the direction of permitted writes depends on which catalog owns the table, which is invisible from the table name. A process holding storage-account credentials can also write files directly to the path that neither catalog ever sees. The result is a table whose row count and history look coherent to each engine separately.
silent_failures.what_evidence_would_catch_it: Name a single writing engine per table and prove it: for Snowflake-managed Iceberg tables, mark the external volume or the storage credential read-only for every other principal; for Unity Catalog paths, use the 'Limit to read-only use' setting on the storage credential and the external location, and align cloud-native RBAC with the Unity Catalog grants (CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE and CREATE EXTERNAL VOLUME are separate from CREATE MANAGED LOCATION). Then reconcile the catalog's row count against a direct file scan of the underlying path on a schedule; a divergence proves an ungoverned writer.
